title: hl-node override_gossip_config.json
description: The hl-node gossip override file, as written to the node user's home directory ($HOME/override_gossip_config.json). 🔴 The node reads this file at start; writing it does not change a running node — the change applies at the node's next start. 🔴 An empty or missing root_node_ips stops the node from starting: there is no built-in fallback. Unknown keys MUST be preserved by clients round-tripping this file, so additionalProperties is true.

chain.description: The chain this node runs. Exactly these two spellings. Must match the chain the node itself is started with; a mismatch stops the node from starting.

root_node_ips.description: The peers the node connects to first, in the order the generator ranked them. 🔴 MUST be non-empty: the node cannot start with an empty list. Shorter lists start faster; a long list buys nothing.

try_new_peers.description: Whether the node may discover peers beyond root_node_ips. Whether false together with a multi-entry root list restricts the node to exactly that list is not established.

reserved_peer_ips.description: Peers the node always admits as inbound peers. 🪤 Entries are BARE STRINGS here, unlike root_node_ips, whose entries are {"Ip": "…"} objects. The two arrays in the same file use two different entry shapes; encode and decode them separately.

n_gossip_peers.description: The node's inbound gossip peer limit. Default 8, valid range [8, 100].

split_client_blocks.description: An optional node flag. The key is OMITTED when false rather than written as false; a client SHOULD do the same when it owns the value, and MUST preserve an explicit false that was already present in a file it is round-tripping.

Ipv4.description: A dotted-quad IPv4 literal. IPv6 is out of contract: whether hl-node accepts an IPv6 literal in this file is unverified, so clients MUST reject IPv6 with an explicit error rather than write an untested value into a file that controls whether the node starts.

RootNodeEntry.description: 🪤 An object with a single key `Ip` — capital I, lowercase p. The spelling is load-bearing. It is NOT a bare string, NOT `ip`, and it carries NO port field.
